markdown_content: ## Introduction to Fur Strand Feature in CLO 2025.0 This section introduces the Fur Strand feature in CLO 2025.0, explaining its location in the interface, how it differs from previous fur rendering options, and its compatibility. Key terms include Fur Strand, material types, fabric properties, and render windows. The Fur Strand feature allows users to visualize fur materials directly in the 3D window within CLO. It is accessed through the fabric material type settings in the Object Browser and Property Editor. When a fabric is selected, a yellow highlight indicates the applied piece in the 3D window. In the Property Editor under materials, users can change the fabric type from "Fur Render Only" to "Fur Strand" to enable real-time fur visualization. Important notes include: - Switching from Fur Render to Fur Strand resets all fabric properties, requiring reapplication of presets. - The Fur Strand feature currently works only in Windows versions of CLO; it is not yet available in CLO for Mac. - Fur Strand visualization is supported both in the 3D window and in the render window, allowing consistent viewing without switching back to Fur Render. --- ## Viewing Options for Fur Strand in the 3D Window This section explains the three available Fur Strand visualization modes—Plain, Line, and Cylinder—accessible via User Settings under the 3D section. Each option offers different levels of detail and performance trade-offs for editing and visualization. - **Plain** (default): Displays fur strands as flat planes showing width and length but not thickness or depth. This mode balances performance and visual information, making it suitable for everyday use and fitting sessions. - **Line**: Displays each fur strand as a straight line representing length only, with no width or thickness visible. This mode is ideal for fast editing and adjustments due to its minimal rendering load. - **Cylinder**: Represents each fur strand as a full 3D cylinder, showing length, width, and thickness. This provides the most realistic and detailed visualization but can significantly slow down performance, making it best for final reviews or presentations. Users can switch these modes quickly in User Settings > 3D > Fur Strand Shape to optimize between visual fidelity and software responsiveness depending on their current workflow stage. --- ## Differences Between Fur Strand and Fur Render This section compares the Fur Strand and Fur Render modes, detailing the visual and rendering distinctions and improvements in realism. - Fur Strand offers a more realistic representation of fur behavior in CLO, showing how strands drape and interact with light more naturally. - Fur Render provides a classic fur look but lacks some of the nuanced draping and lighting effects present in Fur Strand. - Both produce beautiful output, but Fur Strand is closer to real-life fur appearance, especially in how strands fall and catch light. - Rendering differences between the two modes are subtle but notable, with Fur Strand delivering improved realism in final renders. --- ## Workflow for Transitioning from Fur Render to Fur Strand This section outlines a practical workflow for users transitioning existing garments from Fur Render Only fabrics to Fur Strand, including preserving fabric properties and managing presets. 1. **Identify Fur Render fabrics:** Select garments or patterns currently using Fur Render Only fabric types. 2. **Copy properties:** Copy fabric properties from Fur Render fabrics. 3. **Switch fabric type:** Change the fabric type to Fur Strand in the Property Editor. 4. **Paste properties:** Paste copied properties into the new Fur Strand fabric. 5. **Apply presets:** Reapply presets such as color and texture as switching resets these properties. 6. **Save fabrics:** Save the new Fur Strand fabrics for reuse across garments. 7. **Apply saved fabrics:** Select patterns and apply saved Fur Strand fabrics to ensure consistent appearance. 8. **Open multiple fabrics:** Load multiple Fur Strand fabric presets simultaneously for comparison or batch editing. 9. **Interactive preview:** Use the interactive preview to verify the appearance and color fidelity of Fur Strand fabrics. This workflow, while somewhat time-consuming, is straightforward and allows users to maintain fabric consistency when moving between rendering modes. --- ## Important Considerations and Limitations - Fur Strand properties reset when switching from Fur Render, so it is necessary to reapply fabric presets. - Currently, Fur Strand is only supported on Windows; Mac users must continue using Fur Render. - The Cylinder visualization mode impacts software performance due to its detailed rendering of every fur strand. - The Line mode is best suited for fast edits, while Plain mode strikes a balance between detail and responsiveness. - Users should save and organize their Fur Strand fabrics carefully to streamline workflows and avoid property loss. --- This structured overview provides detailed instructions and technical explanations for using CLO 2025.0's Fur Strand feature effectively, ensuring users can leverage its capabilities for realistic fur visualization and efficient garment design workflows.
